REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 8, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.
1.
Call to Order
2.
Invocation
The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution.
Invocation
3.

Pledge of Allegiance
4.
Roll Call
5.
Presentations/Appointments
5A.
Presentations
Presentations
6.
Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for comments related to Consent Calendar Items and items not listed on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council/Successor Agency. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.
7A.
Approval of Minutes
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
July 25, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Minutes
7B.
Approval of Registers of Demands
7B.1.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 8, 2019 (COUNCIL).
City Register
7C.
Award of contract for Bid No. 1377-19, Printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts 2019-2020 Fall and Spring postcards (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
8.
Public Hearings
9.
New and Old Business
9A.
Review and consideration of final approval of Parcel Map 82620, a proposal by property owner Pacifica Plaza, LLC, to convert and subdivide an existing commercial office development comprised of four (4) office buildings into thirty (30) commercial office condominium units at the property located at 13005, 13017, 13047, and 13079 Artesia Boulevard, Cerritos, California, 90703. The subject property is zoned Commercial Office Professional (COP) (APN 7008-004-033) (COUNCIL).*
*Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.
Agenda Report
9B.
Review and consideration of final approval of Parcel Map 82274, a proposal by Cerritos West Covenant Group LLC, on behalf of Dayton Hudson Corporation (Target), to subdivide one (1) parcel into two (2) legal and conforming parcels in order to separate the existing vacant Garden Center and adjacent parking area from the main Target retail building parcel located at 11525 South Street, Cerritos, California, 90703. The subject property is zoned Regional Commercial (CR) (APN 7039-020-017) (COUNCIL).*
*Pursuant to Section 15301 and 15315 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.
Agenda Report
9C.
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO APPLY FOR LOAN FUNDING FROM THE WATER REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA (WRD) THROUGH WRD'S WELL CONSTRUCTION AND REHABILITATION LOAN PROGRAM TO FACILITATE THE REHABILITATION OF THE C-1 WELL AND THE C-2 BOOSTER STATION (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9D.
Review and consideration of award of contract for Bid No. 1374-19, Del Amo Boulevard rehabilitation between Norwalk Boulevard and Pioneer Boulevard, Project No. 14713 (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
10.
Legislative Items
10A.
Report on pending legislation.
10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.
Closed Session
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
AUGUST 8, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Russ Cook, Church in Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division, Campers
  in Leadership Training Participants – Madison Michaelis and Mattson Laraneta.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A Proclamation was made as follows:

  Jim and Candy Yee (50th Wedding Anniversary).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Joe Duran spoke in support of reconsideration of the First Responder statue
  concept presented by Ignacio Gomez.

  Janet Beach spoke in support of reconsideration of the First Responder statue
  concept presented by Ignacio Gomez.

  Rosalie Duran spoke in support of reconsideration of the First Responder
  statue concept presented by Ignacio Gomez.

  Chris Aafedt expressed concerns regarding noise impacts of commercial
  vehicles on Bloomfield Avenue.

  Margaret Rivera expressed concern regarding an unpainted, unmarked
  crosswalk close to City Hall.

  Charles Jordan expressed concerns regarding noise impacts of commercial
  vehicles on Bloomfield Avenue.

  Ruby Martinez expressed concerns regarding noise impacts of commercial
  vehicles on Bloomfield Avenue.
 City of Cerritos  August 8, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Len Goldsmith spoke in support of reconsideration of the First Responder
  statue concept presented by Ignacio Gomez.

  Herman spoke in support of the Los Angeles County Sheriff. He expressed
  concerns regarding lack of reasonable accommodations for those with
  disabilities. He noted he has 1st Amendment rights to free speech.

  Artellia Johnson requested an item regarding the lease of the Mullikin Building
  to be placed on an upcoming agenda. She expressed concerns with lack of
  transparency in the conduct of City business.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  July 25, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of July 25, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 8, 2019
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  8/08/2019  $14,659,878.35 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for Bid No. 1377-19, Printing of the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts 2019-2020 Fall and Spring postcards (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration at the
  request of Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama.

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager.
 City of Cerritos  August 8, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Award a contract for the printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts
  2019-2020 Season Fall and Spring postcards to Advantage Mailing, Inc., Bid
  No. 1377-19, in the amount of $19,144.18; and
  2. In the event issues of non-performance arise, the project would be removed
  from Advantage Mailing, Inc. and taken to the next lowest bidder to ensure
  the City’s printing deadline, quality standards and specifications are met. This
  process would be repeated as necessary in order of the lowest bid to the
  highest (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of final approval of Parcel Map 82620, a proposal by
  property owner Pacifica Plaza, LLC, to convert and subdivide an existing
  commercial office development comprised of four (4) office buildings into thirty
  (30) commercial office condominium units at the property located at 13005,
  13017, 13047, and 13079 Artesia Boulevard, Cerritos, California, 90703. The
  subject property is zoned Commercial Office Professional (COP) (APN 7008-004-
  033) (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this
  project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Herman expressed concern with the tax assessment and CEQA impacts of the
  proposed action.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.
 City of Cerritos  August 8, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Yokoyama, to receive, file, and
  authorize recordation of Parcel Map No. 82620, a proposal by property owner
  Pacifica Plaza, LLC, to convert and subdivide an existing commercial office
  development comprised of four (4) office buildings into thirty (30) commercial office
  condominium units at the property located at 13005, 13017, 13047, and 13079
  Artesia Boulevard, Cerritos, California, 90703, (APN 7008-004-033), subject to the
  final approval by the City Engineer. The subject property is zoned Commercial Office
  Professional (COP) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of final approval of Parcel Map 82274, a proposal by
  Cerritos West Covenant Group LLC, on behalf of Dayton Hudson Corporation
  (Target), to subdivide one (1) parcel into two (2) legal and conforming parcels in
  order to separate the existing vacant Garden Center and adjacent parking area
  from the main Target retail building parcel located at 11525 South Street, Cerritos,
  California, 90703. The subject property is zoned Regional Commercial (CR) (APN
  7039-020-017) (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 and 15315 of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Herman inquired whether the subject project will meet Americans with Disabilities
  Act (ADA) requirements.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to receive, file, and
  authorize recordation of Parcel Map No. 82274, a proposal by Cerritos West
  Covenant Group LLC, on behalf of Dayton Hudson Corporation (Target), to subdivide
  one (1) parcel into two (2) legal and conforming parcels in order to separate the
  existing vacant Garden Center and adjacent parking area from the main Target
  retail building parcel located at 11525 South Street, Cerritos, California, 90703,
  (APN 7039-020-017), subject to the final approval of the City Engineer. The subject
  property is zoned Regional Commercial (CR) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  August 8, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO APPLY FOR
  LOAN FUNDING FROM THE WATER REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT OF SOUTHERN
  CALIFORNIA (WRD) THROUGH WRD’S WELL CONSTRUCTION AND REHABILITATION
  LOAN PROGRAM TO FACILITATE THE REHABILITATION OF THE C-1 WELL AND THE
  C-2 BOOSTER STATION (COUNCIL).
  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Finance Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Paul Bellenbaum inquired regarding potable water levels at the subject site.

  Herman noted that higher population density increases water demand and
  suggested construction of a water recycling facility.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2019-14, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO APPLY FOR LOAN
  FUNDING FROM THE WATER REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT OF SOUTHERN
  CALIFORNIA (WRD) THROUGH WRD’S WELL CONSTRUCTION AND
  REHABILITATION LOAN PROGRAM TO FACILITATE THE REHABILITATION
  OF THE C-1 WELL AND THE C-2 BOOSTER STATION (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of award of contract for Bid No. 1374-19, Del Amo
  Boulevard rehabilitation between Norwalk Boulevard and Pioneer Boulevard, Project
  No. 14713 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1.  Award a contract for the Del Amo Boulevard Rehabilitation – Norwalk
  Boulevard to Pioneer Boulevard, Project No. 14713, Bid No. 1374-19, to GMC
  Engineering in the amount of $1,094,856 to include the following additive
  alternates, and reject all other bids:
  a. Additive alternate #1: Removal of existing trees and roots along Del
  Amo Boulevard within the project area
  b. Additive alternate #2: Installation of pipes and cleanouts for “Green
  Streets” rain water infiltration devices
  c. Additive alternate #4: Landscaping and irrigation improvements
  within the project area; and
 City of Cerritos  August 8, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  (continued)

  2.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Pulido, Mayor Pro
  Tem Yokoyama and Mayor Solanki.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned in memory of Margaret “Maggie” Montgomery at 9:00
  p.m.
